# Seven-base partial-tail and tangent-shape response envelopes

This note gives an attained GLOBAL first-order mixed-depth envelope
for one fixed seven-base source. It includes two distinct limiting
regimes: atomless unscaled canonical marginals, and full-dimensional
microscopic tangent bodies. The latter retains geometric information
that conditional weak point-mass limits lose.

Let T be a full d-simplex, d>=2, with volume V, centroid g,
barycentric coordinates lambda_i and linear parts l_i. Put

    m=d+1, b=1/m, h=d/m, Gamma=h^d,
    kappa=d V h^(d-1).

The integer bases are Q={0,1}^2 and

    r=(-1,0), p=(-1,1), p'=(1,-1).

Put T at each core base, R_t at r, A_t at p and C_t at p'.
All three added convex bodies are contained in T, with volumes

    |R_t|=t w_t, |A_t|=t a_t, |C_t|=t c_t,
    w_t->w>0, a_t->a>0, c_t->c>0.                   (1)

Their convex hull has exactly these actual integer fibers. The
quadrilateral and exposed-base proof is in
candidate 8c889e9b634ca1eb,
independently audited in audit-seven-base-global-partial-trace-depth-helly.md.
Its total mixed mass is M_t=4V+t(w_t+a_t+c_t).

Let D_{6,t}^0 be the maximum absolute depth on the core fiber q=(0,0)
after deleting R_t, i.e. in the six-base source. Let D_{7,t}^0 be
the corresponding seven-base local maximum, and D_{7,t} the true
global maximum over every actual source point.

## 1. Exact local reduction for all sufficiently small added bodies

For ALL families satisfying (1), without any weak-limit assumptions,
there is a fixed neighborhood U of g such that, for sufficiently
small t and every y in U,

    A_{7,t}((q,y))=t w_t+A_{6,t}((q,y)).             (2)

Consequently, for sufficiently small t,

    D_{7,t}^0=t w_t+D_{6,t}^0,                      (3)

and the two local maximizing-point sets coincide EXACTLY.

For proof use the positive simplex profile rho_d from
tiny-contained-endpoint-has-exact-mixed-simplex-depth.md. Define

    F(y,u)=|T intersect {u.x>=u.y}|,
    Q(y,u)=|T intersect {u.x>=2u.y-min_T u.x}|.

Both are jointly continuous for y near g and unit u, including
supporting thresholds, and F(g,u)+Q(g,u)>=(Gamma+rho_d)V.
By compactness there is one neighborhood U such that

    F(y,u)+Q(y,u)>=(Gamma+rho_d/2)V
                     for y in U and every unit u.  (4)

If a nonvertical through-(q,y) cap does not fully capture R_t,
its threshold at r is above min_T u.x. Its opposite core partner
at (1,0) has threshold below 2u.y-min_T u.x. The own fiber and
this partner therefore pay at least (4). Vertical through-q
caps pay at least V, also strictly above this level.

On the other hand, the exact bounded-tilt construction in
candidate 1ec867c146e96dba,
Section 1, realizes ANY pair shift while excluding every other
core fiber. Its coefficients beta_1=-K+s/2,beta_2=-K-s/2 also
capture ALL R_t at r: beta.r=K-s/2>=diam(T)+1, whereas
u.(x-y)>=-diam(T) on T. Thus the six-base minimizing cap has a
seven-base realization of cost exactly A_{6,t}((q,y))+t w_t.
This cost is at most

    Gamma V+t(w_t+min(a_t,c_t)),                    (5)

because at any y in T one canonical own cap costs at most Gamma V
and a saturated shift pays only the smaller added mass. For small
t, (5) is strictly below (4). Every cap that might improve the
minimum must therefore fully capture R_t. Such a cap costs at
least t w_t plus the exact six-base minimum. This proves (2).

The canonical upper caps also give O(t) localization of ALL local
maximizers in both sources, exactly as in the six-base note:
their depth at g is at least Gamma V, and their canonical own
caps have added cost bounded by t(w_t+a_t+c_t). Their barycentric
coordinates differ from b by O(t). They therefore lie in U for
small t. Equation (2) then proves (3) and equality of their full
maximizing sets. This reasoning introduces no convergence rate
for the added shapes.

## 2. Exact global reduction and strict base classification

The other anchors (0,1),(1,0) have exact local maxima
Gamma V+t a_t and Gamma V+t c_t, uniquely at their own g, for
small t. The contained-endpoint theorem gives their lower bounds;
the isolators delta_01=z_1+2(1-z_2) and delta_10=1-z_1+z_2
give the matching upper caps while excluding the added R_t.
The core (1,1) has local maximum Gamma V. Exposed vertical caps
bound all added-base depths by their O(t) fiber volumes.
Therefore the exact finite-t global identity is

    D_{7,t}=Gamma V+max{t a_t,t c_t,
                         t w_t+D_{6,t}^0-Gamma V}. (6)

Below, suppose D_{6,t}^0=Gamma V+t Jbar+o(t). Then

    D_{7,t}=Gamma V+t L+o(t),
    L=max{a,c,w+Jbar},                              (7)
    D_{7,t}/M_t=Gamma/4
       +t[4L-Gamma(w+a+c)]/(16V)+o(t).              (8)

If w+Jbar>max(a,c), every global maximizer lies at base q and
has the local displacement given below. If a>max(c,w+Jbar),
the unique global maximizer is ((0,1),g); similarly for c.
When leading coefficients tie, (7) does not decide the global
maximizing set without higher-order or exact source information.

## 3. Atomless unscaled partial-tail regime

Suppose the normalized laws of A_t,C_t converge weakly to nu,omega
and both give zero mass to EVERY hyperplane {lambda_i=r}, for
every canonical i and every real threshold r. Define

    J_i=min_s[a nu{lambda_i>=b+s}
                         +c omega{lambda_i>=b-s}],
    Jbar=(1/m)sum_i J_i.                            (9)

The scalar minima are attained on a fixed compact interval. Then
(7)-(8) hold and every maximizing point of the q fiber satisfies

    y_t=g+t v_*+o(t),
    l_i(v_*)=(J_i-Jbar)/kappa.                      (10)

The full proof is the six-base partial-tail theorem. Allowing
a_t,c_t to converge instead of being fixed only adds o(1) to
its optimized partial-tail term, because all probabilities lie
in [0,1]. The uniform moving-normal/shift proof and O(t)
localization are unchanged. Equations (2)-(3) then transfer the
attained local response and every maximizing selection exactly.

## 4. Microscopic tangent bodies: a different, proved response regime

Instead assume

    A_t=g+epsilon_t B_t, C_t=g+epsilon_t E_t,
    epsilon_t=t^(1/d),
    B_t->B, E_t->E in Hausdorff distance,             (11)

where B,E are full-dimensional convex bodies. The prelimit bodies
are convex and the convergence is in the original continuous
coordinates; translations are part of B_t,E_t and are not dropped.
For small t the added bodies lie in T since g is interior and
the tangent bodies are uniformly bounded. Their masses in (1)
satisfy a_t=|B_t|->|B|=a, c_t=|E_t|->|E|=c.

The correct coefficients in this regime are

    J_i=min_sigma [|B intersect {l_i>=sigma}|
                             +|E intersect {l_i>=-sigma}|],
    Jbar=(1/m)sum_i J_i.                            (12)

The minima are attained. Formulas (7)-(8) and (10) hold with
these J_i. In particular, conditional weak limits delta_g have
been replaced by actual tangent-shape cap data.

Here are the full convergence details. In a continuous unit
direction u at y, write the pair shift as s=epsilon_t sigma.
The added cap sum divided by t is exactly

    |B_t intersect {u.x>=tau_t+sigma}|
       +|E_t intersect {u.x>=tau_t-sigma}|,
    tau_t=u.(y-g)/epsilon_t.                        (13)

Every maximizing y is O(t) from g, and the trial points used for
the lower bound have that same bound. Since d>=2,

    tau_t=O(t^(1-1/d))->0.                          (14)

This is the precise reason d=1 is excluded from this microscopic
formula: there the candidate displacement would remain in (13).

Choose a common ball of radius R containing all B_t,E_t,B,E.
Once |tau_t|<=1, shifts |sigma|>R+1 give the saturated costs
|B_t| or |E_t|, already obtained at the endpoints. Thus all minima
in (13) lie in a common compact shift interval. Hausdorff convergence
of full-dimensional convex bodies gives L1 convergence of their
indicators: points in the interior of the limiting body are
eventually inside, points outside eventually outside, and the
boundary has Lebesgue measure zero. All lie in a common ball.

If u_t tends to a canonical unit normal and sigma_t converges,
the moving halfspace indicators converge off a single hyperplane,
which has zero volume for B and E. Combining this with the L1
body convergence and (14) proves convergence of (13) to its
limiting cap sum. A compactness subsequence proves uniformity
over the entire shift interval, hence convergence of minima.
The normalization from unit u_i to l_i is harmless because sigma
is free. No Hausdorff convergence rate relative to t is required.

The remainder of the all-normal proof is exactly the simplex
response argument: an approximately minimizing direction must
approach one of the canonical directions; the unperturbed own
excess stays nonnegative; its smooth first variation is
-kappa l_i(v); and the optimized added term tends to J_i. The
finite balance max_v min_i(J_i-kappa l_i(v))=Jbar gives the lower
bound, averaging the canonical upper caps gives the upper bound,
and the zero-sum argument gives every maximizing displacement.
This proves the microscopic response completely, including
normal motion and compact attainment of its partial-tail costs.

Centered homothetic simplex tangents B=E with volume a have
J_i=2Gamma a for every i; centrally symmetric tangents centered
at zero have J_i=a. Thus (12) recovers the two exact global
coefficient families of the contributor's seven-base note, while also
allowing nonsymmetric tangent translations and anisotropic data.

## 5. An all-dimensional example with genuine global center motion

Take T=conv(0,e_1,...,e_d). In the microscopic regime let

    B_t=E_t=[0,1]^d,
    A_t=C_t=R_t=g+t^(1/d)[0,1]^d.                  (15)

All three added volumes are exactly t, so a=c=w=1. These bodies
are contained in T whenever t^(1/d)<1/[d(d+1)]. The actual
seven-base compatibility is already proved in the setup.

For i=1,...,d, the tangent l_i coordinate is x_i on the unit cube.
Its two opposite-threshold tails about zero have minimum one:
one cap is full when the other becomes proper or empty, and a
saturated threshold attains one. For i=0, l_0=-sum_j x_j, and
at shift zero both tangent caps have zero d-volume. Thus

    J_0=0, J_1=...=J_d=1, Jbar=d/(d+1),
    v_*=(1/[m kappa],...,1/[m kappa]).               (16)

Since w+Jbar=1+d/(d+1)>1=max(a,c), EVERY global maximizer for
small t has the single integer base q=(0,0), and

    D_{7,t}=Gamma V+t[1+d/(d+1)]+o(t),
    y_t=g+t v_*+o(t).                              (17)

This does not assert uniqueness of the continuous maximizer at
each positive t. It specifies every maximizer's first-order motion.
At the original g the local value is exactly Gamma V+t for small
t: the six-base canonical l_0 cap at zero shift misses both small
positive-orthant cubes, and the owned R_t is then paid by the
exact identity (2). The other two anchor centroids also have
depth Gamma V+t. Hence all prescribed core centroids are strictly
suboptimal, while the moving point at q wins at first order.

The source remains above the OC target. The result is a concrete
global partial-trace allocation and deterministic-center response
for this seven-base geometry, not a general selection rule.

## 6. Exact verification scope

../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_seven_base_tangent_response.py uses only the Python standard
library. It verifies 12 exact moving-candidate canonical expansions
in dimension two, 96 exact proper-pair minima with the same bounded
base tilt capturing the owned fiber and strictly excluding other
core fibers, and 29 exact dimensional balances for d=2,...,30.
The planar scalar minimizations inspect every vertex-event cell
and its quadratic critical point. The compactness, perturbation,
all-normal, and all-dimensional conclusions are proved above.
